The witness pair has identical explicit histograms for the six necessary lengths and distinct canonical dihedral representatives. Complete word enumeration 2^n for every n<=12, with two independently constructed exact implementations, gives the observed 224 classes and 223 spectra and the unique two-bracelet class; checker output VERIFY_OK. Moment expansion proves that the full histograms imply homometry and the CSV exhaustively documents all 23 homometric pairs. The 12-periodic lift for all powers is proved algebraically, not inferred from the five tested powers. No larger-length uniqueness claim is made.

originality.rationale: The 2011 cyclic Z-relation work establishes the interval-vector/Patterson autocorrelation and earlier homometric collisions; it does not specify the complete distributions of all cyclic consecutive-window weights. Jedrzejewski--Johnson (2013) enumerate 19 homometric pairs of length twelve for weights <=6, which becomes 23 at all weights, but do not filter them by the much stronger full cyclic window multiset. Acharya et al. (2014) analyze linear contiguous substrings, not cyclic wrapping windows. The two observed source frameworks are mathematically distinct from the 224-to-223 cyclic bracelet quotient proved here. Searches under cyclic Parikh-window compositions, sliding-window sums, circular reconstructibility, Z-relation, and necklaces found no implication covering the exact earliest noninjectivity, pair classification, or infinite periodic lift. Historical unindexed equivalence remains a substantive residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed earlier formulation using circular scan-statistics, cyclic sliding-window sums, or genomic circular composition profiles could subsume this result.

Published homometry tables give the coarser exact 23-pair baseline but do not establish uniqueness of the strong-spectrum survivor; verifying an unpublished refinement might affect historical priority.

value.rationale: A sharp first failure of injectivity and complete first-collision classification are naturally motivated exact reconstruction invariants. Demonstrating that full cyclic consecutive-window statistics eliminate 22 of 23 previously known length-twelve two-point-homometric ambiguities quantifies higher-order information absent from pairwise measurement. The explicit periodic-power construction shows genuine noninjectivity at infinitely many lengths. Unlike the known linear substring problem this is a different, circular data model, not a reparameterized prior computation. Scientific importance is bounded: full asymptotic ambiguity behavior is not established.
